name: AIRBTC escrow's done() pays out any token to any caller
summary: The unverified AIRBTC escrow contract's done(string,uint256,address) transfers a caller-chosen amount of the named coin from the escrow to a caller-chosen address without checking the caller; the project's router used it for user payouts. MEV bots replaying a user's claim first took 2.424 USDT each through it, then an attacker had it send the escrow's 1.01e9 AIRBTC to its contract and sold them into the AIRBTC/USDT pair for 6,818 USDT.
notes: Anchor: the escrow's first outflow not routed through the project's router 0x4ab0127d is bot 0xec48dace's done() call at block 42145133, index 1, which took 2.424 USDT while replaying user 0x14ad3d37's claim; 24 more bot calls in blocks 42145133-42145137 did the same, the DeFiHackLabs transaction 0x00e4bbc8 drained the AIRBTC ten hours later, and 0x101723de took the last 90.4 USDT. Campaign: every escrow outflow transaction (Etherscan token transfers) not sent to the router.

Loss: the bots' 25 done() payouts (60.6 USDT) and 0x101723de's 90.4 USDT, plus the escrow's 1,009,907,600 AIRBTC valued at the 6,833.24 USDT its sale drew from the pair, since the dump crashed the price (rule 12). The 20.2 USDT releases the bots' replays sent to the user are not counted.

Reset: deployment. The owner's authFromContract (0x5f5750e3, 83 blocks later) wired the router and helper addresses into slots 0x10 and 0x1d-0x20; the code is unverified, so whether done() reads them is unconfirmed, and taking it as the reset would shorten the 11.5-day age by four minutes.
